title: Fibre-generic valuation sets and modification locus
statement: Let $C,Y,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $c:C\to T$ and $q:Y\to C$. For each generic point $g$ of an irreducible component of $C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], put $L_g=\kappa(g)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and use the centred valuation points $(O,\operatorname{Spec}O\to C)$ restricting to the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}L_g\to C$ [def-trf-riemann-zariski-generic-models] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define $\mathcal V(C)$ as the disjoint union of these existing types, with the disjoint-union topology of their centre-projection topologies [def-trf-birational-valuation-neighbourhood-data]. For reduced $C$, $L_g$ is the function field of its component. Define $\Gamma(q,c)$ to consist of valuations admitting a lift $l:\operatorname{Spec}O\to Y$ over $C$ whose closed-point image is a generic point of an irreducible component of a scheme-theoretic fibre of $q$ followed by $c$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Define $\Gamma_0(q,c)$ to be its subset whose original centre on $C$ is closed in $C$. For a modification [def-trf-modification] the proper lift is unique. Use the isomorphism open $\operatorname{IsoOpen}(q)$, the union of all opens $U\subset C$ over which the actual restriction of $q$ is an isomorphism [def-nagata-maximal-isomorphism-open]. Its complement is closed; define the modification-locus ideal as its vanishing ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], so the associated closed subscheme is the reduced induced modification locus.
